objective: site selection MCDA for a sweets-first QSR format in Kolkata

layers.name: Residential Population
layers.whyItMatters: Proximity to residential areas increases potential walk-in customers.

layers.name: Food Cluster Whitespace & Ecosystem
layers.whyItMatters: Identifying areas with less food competition can capture unmet demand.

layers.name: Road Visibility & Commercial Frontage
layers.whyItMatters: High visibility increases brand awareness and foot traffic.

layers.name: Affinity POIs - Temples/Markets
layers.whyItMatters: Proximity to affinity POIs can drive additional foot traffic.

layers.name: Delivery Catchment Density
layers.whyItMatters: Larger delivery catchment increases potential delivery orders.

layers.name: Transit Proximity
layers.whyItMatters: Proximity to transit nodes increases accessibility for customers.

layers.name: Daytime Generators
layers.whyItMatters: Nearby daytime population can boost lunch-time sales.

layers.name: Apartment Cluster Density
layers.whyItMatters: Dense apartment clusters indicate potential customer base.

feasibility.explanation: The study area and layers are well-defined with no conflicting constraints.

assumptions.assumption: Study area includes Chinar Park, Salt Lake, Sector V, and Newtown in Kolkata.
assumptions.basis: User specified bounding box covering these areas.

misleadingVariables.risk: Irrelevant at 500m scale for micro-market analysis.
Vehicular traffic does not equate to pedestrian footfall.

scenarios.name: Balanced
scenarios.description: Equal emphasis on residential and commercial factors.

validation: Compare model scores at locations of established chains (McDonald's, Haldiram's outlets) — they should score above median.
modelFailureRisks: OSM residential counts may understate informal settlements, affecting catchment analysis.
